Class VisibilityDomainPruning

java.lang.Object
org.locationtech.geomesa.trino.security.VisibilityDomainPruning
public final class VisibilityDomainPruning extends Object
Builds Domain constraints on the visibility column that Iceberg's own per-file manifest statistics (min/max, null-count) can use to prune whole files before any row is read — a necessary-condition pre-filter that runs ALONGSIDE, and never in place of, the always-enforced is_visible() row filter installed by VisibilityAccessControl.

Direction of error. A domain here only narrows the set of candidate files; it can never widen it. So a wrong or overly-narrow domain can only make a query wrongly omit rows the caller was entitled to see (a correctness/availability bug) — it can never cause a row the row filter would have hidden to be returned (never a security/leak bug). That asymmetry is what bounds the blast radius of an incomplete expressionDomain(VarcharType, Set, Set) candidate universe (see below) to a correctness bug rather than a leak.

Unrestricted rows always survive pruning. A NULL or empty ("") visibility carries no real expression and is unrestricted — is_visible() returns true for it, so the row filter returns it to every caller (see GeoMesaSecurityFunctions.isVisible(Slice, Slice)). Every domain this class builds therefore admits BOTH NULL and "" (see unrestrictedDomain(VarcharType)); otherwise a file holding only unrestricted rows could be pruned even though the row filter would have returned them — a correctness bug. In particular "" must be admitted explicitly: it can never be a declared candidate (the connector drops blank entries), so nothing else would add it.

Which way "wrong" cuts for expressionDomain(VarcharType, Set, Set). Its declared candidate universe must be COMPLETE to be sound. Over-declaring is harmless: a declared value that never occurs simply never matches, so pruning is merely weaker. Under-declaring is the dangerous direction: because the domain is a positive IN-list, a value that actually occurs but is omitted is never admitted, so a file holding only that value is over-pruned — a caller whose auths actually admit it silently loses those rows (a correctness/ availability bug). Still never a leak, per the invariant above; but an incomplete universe prunes too MUCH, not too little.

  • Method Details

    • emptyAuthsDomain

      public static Optional<io.trino.spi.predicate.Domain> emptyAuthsDomain(io.trino.spi.type.VarcharType visColumnType, Set<String> auths)
      Sound unconditionally, for any visibility expression grammar: an identity with no authorizations can be granted access only to an unrestricted visibility (NULL or "") — AccessEvaluator never grants a non-empty expression to an empty auth set, no matter how simple or compound it is (see GeoMesaSecurityFunctions.isVisible(Slice, Slice)). So when auths is empty the only rows the caller could ever see are the unrestricted ones, and Iceberg can prune any file that holds neither a "" value nor a NULL for the column.
      Parameters:
      visColumnType - the visibility column's type (always VARCHAR)
      auths - the resolved authorizations for the querying identity
      Returns:
      an unrestricted-only domain (NULL or "") when auths is empty; empty Optional otherwise (an empty result is not a signal to fall back — see expressionDomain(VarcharType, Set, Set) for the non-empty-auths case)

    • expressionDomain

      public static Optional<io.trino.spi.predicate.Domain> expressionDomain(io.trino.spi.type.VarcharType visColumnType, Set<String> candidateExpressions, Set<String> auths)
      Sound for ANY visibility expression grammar, compound included: this prunes on literal expression VALUES via the real is_visible() decision rather than on decomposed tokens. candidateExpressions is the closed universe of every distinct non-null value the visibility column can ever hold (e.g. a declared ladder: "basic", "basic&privileged", ...); each one is run through the real GeoMesaSecurityFunctions.isVisible(Slice, Slice) decision — the identical engine the row filter uses — so "does the caller's auth set admit this literal string" is answered exactly, with no token-vs-expression mismatch for &/| to fall through.

      Soundness therefore reduces to completeness of candidateExpressions, and completeness is REQUIRED, not best-effort: a value present in the column but omitted here is never added to the admitted set, so a file holding only that value is pruned even for a caller whose auths would admit it — silently dropping rows they were entitled to (a correctness/availability bug). This never leaks (the domain only narrows the file set; the is_visible() row filter still runs), but under-declaring prunes too MUCH, not too little. Over-declaring is safe: a declared value that never occurs simply never matches. Scales to tens-to-low-hundreds of distinct values; not intended for effectively-unique per-row visibility strings.

      The admitted set always includes the unrestricted values (NULL and "") on top of the auth-admissible declared expressions, so unrestricted rows are never pruned regardless of the caller's auths. When no declared expression is admissible, the domain collapses to the unrestricted-only set (NULL or ""), identical to emptyAuthsDomain(VarcharType, Set).

      Parameters:
      visColumnType - the visibility column's type (always VARCHAR)
      candidateExpressions - every distinct non-null value the column can hold
      auths - the resolved authorizations for the querying identity
      Returns:
      an IN-list-plus-unrestricted (NULL/"") domain over the expressions auths can access; empty Optional when auths or candidateExpressions is empty (use emptyAuthsDomain(VarcharType, Set) for the former)
